describes: The town's house paints and how a coat ages: the era palettes (each paint its own value, chroma and hue, planned in grey first: docs/research/masters-of-colour.md, Designed places), which paint a house wears when no record names one, how often a kept house was repainted before the engine's people start (the pack's past), and the weather that wears a wall by its aspect. Colours are CIE LCh read at the paint's own L* as a fresh coat in neutral light; a coat's age moves them by its material (materials/paint-*.json, chalk).
provenance: Authored, 28 October 2026. Values planned in grey (L*) first, then hue and chroma by the rules in masters-of-colour.md (white chosen not tinted; earth paints near C* 30 to 45; accents rare and from facts); ox-red from Stavanger's sea houses (photo 01's neighbours, the research's wooden-town-architecture.md); unverified against paint charts. Lightness from measured sources since 29 October 2026 (r09): each paint's `source`, which says where it is only an estimate or none was found.

wall_white_linseed.describes: Linseed-oil white: high, a little warm, yellowing as it ages.
wall_white_linseed.source: L: measured, titanium white in linseed on spruce, fresh, L* 92.0 (b* +9.6), spectrophotometer 45/0, D65/10 deg (Baar, Mácová, Hess, Zárybnická, Dvořák, 'Natural weathering of linseed oil paints', WCTE 2025, pp. 5654-5661, doi:10.52202/080513-0697, Table 4). No lead or zinc white in linseed was found measured. C and h are not yet from it (the measured b* +9.6 is warmer than C 3).

wall_white.describes: The 1980s titanium alkyd white: chalk-fresh, neutral, the brightest thing in the street.
wall_white.source: L: estimate, not measured: Jotun 9918 Klassisk hvit, hex F0EFEA (paintdb.com) gives L* 94.4, Jotun 1001 Egghvit, hex EFEDE3 (jotun.com) gives 93.7; no measured titanium alkyd white was found.

wall_oxred.describes: Ox-red iron oxide in linseed: deep, warm, chalking to a dusty pink-brown with the decades.
wall_oxred.source: Measured, a natural iron-oxide red earth (Terra Pozzuoli) in linseed on spruce, fresh: L* 39.0, a* 28.1, b* 21.0 (C* 35.1, h 37); after 5 years outdoors L* 39.9, C* 27.8, h 37 (Baar, Mácová, Hess, Zárybnická, Dvořák, 'Natural weathering of linseed oil paints', WCTE 2025, pp. 5654-5661, doi:10.52202/080513-0697, Table 4). Beside it: the Falu red code NCS S 5040-Y80R matched by Taubmans at LRV 9.34 (L* 36.6, bimcontent.com), Jotun 0154 Ætterød hex 824A43 (L* 37.9, an estimate).

wall_ochre.source: Measured, ferric oxide yellow in linseed on spruce, fresh: L* 54.0, a* 17.7, b* 42.0 (C* 45.6, h 67) (Baar, Mácová, Hess, Zárybnická, Dvořák, 'Natural weathering of linseed oil paints', WCTE 2025, pp. 5654-5661, doi:10.52202/080513-0697, Table 4). A lightened mix such as Jotun 0738 Herregårdsgul is about L* 67 (hex D09951, an estimate).

wall_greygreen.source: None found: authored, unverified. The nearest measured greens (ECOSTRESS olive alkyd gloss 0385-0408, L* 47.5-48.4, C* 23; chromium oxide green in linseed, L* 41.6) are other colours.

trim_white_linseed.describes: The trims' white, as the wall's.
trim_white_linseed.source: As wall_white_linseed: L* 92.0 measured (Baar, Mácová, Hess, Zárybnická, Dvořák, 'Natural weathering of linseed oil paints', WCTE 2025, pp. 5654-5661, doi:10.52202/080513-0697, Table 4).

trim_white.source: As wall_white: L* 93.7-94.4, an estimate from Jotun's hex colours, not measured.

defaults.describes: The paint a house wears when no 'repainted' event names one: by its era and kind, the wall's and the trims'. A warehouse's trims stay white on any wall (the sea houses' white casings on ox-red).

upkeep.describes: Before the engine's people start (pack.json peopleStart) a kept house was repainted every so many years by its wealth: the poor less often (the cycle at wealth 0 and at 1000, linear); a neglect or a boarding stops it. The last coat before a house is let go is the cycle's last turn before that year, counted from the house's building, so it is the house's own.
upkeep.white: a coat's colour after the cycle: the default paint, unless a 'repainted' event names one

derived.describes: From peopleStart care is the keeper's (docs/engine-requests.md 13). Until the engine exports keepers, blender/parts/street/care.py derives each building's coats from its record and writes them into the fixture as 'repainted' events with provenance 'derived': each turn the pack's cycle by the house's wealth, longer by absentFactor when the keeper does not live there (a type not in livedIn: a warehouse's firm or landlord), each turn's length seeded within jitter of it; a recorded repaint resets the turn, a neglect or a boarding ends it. absentFactor is our reading, unverified.

weather.describes: Where the rain comes from: Stavanger's wet winds blow from the south and south-west off the sea (pack frame: x east, y north). A wall's exposure is how squarely it faces them, from `least` on the lee to 1; a gable takes the wind's rain on its whole height.
